subject: Re: Pricing + batching/concurrency assumptions — follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@vela.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing + batching/concurrency assumptions — follow-up

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the call today — great to learn more about Vela.ai's search and summarization use cases. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the assumptions we used on token volumes and batching so the pricing estimate aligns with your expected workload. Please see the items below and correct anything I mis-stated.

Summary of current assumptions:
- Monthly active users: ~120k (peak 20% daily activity)
- Average request size: ~450 tokens (prompt + expected generation)
- Average responses per user per month: 35
- Estimated monthly tokens: ~1.9B tokens (approx)
- Target unit economics: $X / 1M tokens (we discussed a target in the $6–$10 range)

Batching + concurrency details we discussed:
- Workload pattern: continuous steady traffic with short peaks (20–30 minute bursts during product updates)
- Prefer continuous batching (we’ll accept a small latency tail for better throughput)
- Expected concurrency: ~120–250 concurrent inference requests at peak (mostly short-LLM calls, <2s generation)
- Many requests share similar prefixes (search context), so prefix caching could help reduce cost

Next steps / asks for Vela:
1) Can you confirm the monthly tokens and whether the 1.9B estimate aligns with your finance model?
2) Would you share a 24-hour traffic sample (csv) showing timestamps and request sizes so we can model batching efficiency and latency?
3) Confirm target $/1M tokens or budget range for a committed plan (so we can propose Dedicated vs Hosted pricing).

I'll attach a preliminary pricing workbook with two scenarios (hosted pay-as-you-go and 12-mo committed Dedicated). Aditya, Marissa — looping you in to help with quantization and continuous-batching assumptions if Alice shares the traffic sample.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx

From: Alice Chen <alice@vela.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Victor Lin <victor@vela.ai>, Procurement <procurement@vela.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing + batching/concurrency assumptions — follow-up

Thanks Camila — this looks right directionally. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Monthly tokens: our finance model currently shows ~1.6B tokens/month but with product growth runway to ~2.4B in 9–12 months. So please model both 1.6B and 2.4B scenarios.
- Budget: procurement is comfortable with a target of $8 / 1M tokens for committed pricing; if the economics support it, there's room to go lower for a multi-year committed deal.
- Concurrency: the 120–250 range is accurate for user-facing endpoints. We also have internal batch jobs (off-hours) that can be run at lower priority — those could be scheduled to take advantage of cheaper windows.

I attached a 24-hr sample of request timestamps and token sizes (vela-traffic-sample.csv). The sample shows fairly even traffic across the day with two modest peaks at 10:00 and 16:00 PT.

Happy to schedule the technical deep-dive next week. Victor will coordinate.

On Mon, Jun 21, 2026 at 08:15 AM Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call — attaching the workbook now.
>
Best,
Alice

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@vela.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Victor Lin <victor@vela.ai>, Procurement <procurement@vela.ai>
Date: 2026-06-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing + batching/concurrency assumptions — follow-up

Perfect — thanks for the sample, Alice. I reviewed the CSV and had a few follow-ups so our continuous-batching model is accurate: 

1) Average tokens per request in sample: ~420 (prompt + response). We'll model 420/450 to bracket scenarios.
2) The traffic shape is good for continuous batching — with even distribution and short peaks, we expect batching efficiency of ~1.6–2.2x token reduction depending on how many requests share prefixes and whether we can group similar sequence-length requests.
3) Concurrency modeling: based on the sample, observed 95th percentile concurrency is ~180. For safety we'll model both 150 and 225 peaks.

Questions for Vela (small asks):
- Can you confirm if internal batch jobs are flexible to run in a maintenance window (e.g., midnight–4am PT)? If yes, we can schedule heavy quantized workloads there and reflect lower unit costs.
- Any SLAs required for user-facing endpoints (p95 latency target)? This affects choice between Hosted SLO-backed routes vs Dedicated pools.

What we'll deliver by next Tuesday (6/29):
- Updated pricing workbook with 1.6B and 2.4B scenarios and target $8/1M token committed options
- Continuous-batching efficiency model (assumptions clearly stated)
- Recommendation: Hosted vs Dedicated with cost/latency tradeoffs and autoscaling knobs

Aditya & Marissa: can you review the batching assumptions and add comments in the sheet (drive link above)? I flagged the rows where prefix caching and quantization assumptions apply.

Thanks,
Camila

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-23T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing + batching/concurrency assumptions — follow-up

Quick notes from infra/quant side: 
- Continuous batching: with the traffic sample, we should assume an average batching window of 50–120ms for user-facing traffic, which yields good throughput without blowing up p95. We'll include a sensitivity sweep at 30ms, 75ms, 120ms.
- Expected effective token savings: 1.5x baseline for heterogeneous requests, up to 2.3x in best-case similar-prefix scenarios. Use conservative 1.6x for the initial committed pricing model.
- Concurrency headroom: assuming Dedicated pools sized for 225 concurrency at peak, we have comfortable room for autoscaling and graceful degradation to a second-tier model variant (lower-cost quantized) if capacity constrained.

I'll add these to the workbook and comment on the quantization rows.

-Aditya

From: Alice Chen <alice@vela.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Victor Lin <victor@vela.ai>, Procurement <procurement@vela.ai>
Date: 2026-06-25T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing + batching/concurrency assumptions — follow-up

Thanks Camila and team — this is great. A couple final notes before the technical deep-dive: 

- Procurement confirms the $8 / 1M tokens target for a 12-month committed plan; finance will expect a clear per-token math with breakpoints at 1.6B and 2.4B.
- We can move internal batch jobs to midnight–4am PT as suggested. That should unlock better quantization and lower unit costs.
- SLA: p95 latency target for user endpoints is 450ms. If Dedicated pools are required to meet that at peak, please call it out explicitly in the recommendation.

Let's plan the tech deep-dive for Wednesday 6/30 — Victor will send a calendar invite with an agenda (include sample traffic, the workbook, and a short infra slide).

Looking forward —
Alice

Attachment: SOC2-questionnaire.pdf
